title: Mom's Camping Packing List
text:
Mom made a packing list for our camping trip. She taped it to the fridge with a {adjective} magnet so nobody would forget anything.

1. One tent. Last year we forgot the poles, so we slept under a {noun} instead.
2. Three sleeping bags and a pillow shaped like a {animal}.
3. Twelve {plural noun} for roasting over the campfire.
4. Bug spray. Dad says mosquitoes love to {verb} {adverb} near his ears.
5. A flashlight, in case the moon is too {adjective}.
6. Grandpa's lucky {noun}. He has brought it on every trip since he was {number} years old.

At the bottom, Dad added one more thing in big letters: DO NOT PACK THE {plural noun}. Mom says that is a long story, and it has a canoe and a very {adjective} raccoon in it.

title: Ranger Bob's Campfire Rules
text:
Welcome to Pine Cone Campground! Ranger Bob wrote these campfire rules. Please read them before you sit down to {verb}.

Rule 1: Only grown-ups may light the fire. Kids may help by holding the {noun} and cheering {adverb}.
Rule 2: Sit on a log, not on a {noun}. We learned this the hard way last summer.
Rule 3: Marshmallows should be golden brown. If yours turns {color}, please tell a ranger right away.
Rule 4: Campfire songs are allowed until {number} o'clock. The song about the {adjective} moose is our favorite.
Rule 5: Do not feed the campfire any {plural noun}. It makes the smoke smell like {food}.

At the end of the night, a grown-up will pour water on the fire. Everyone must wave and tell the fire goodnight {adverb}. Ranger Bob says the fire gets very {adjective} if you forget.

title: Dear Diary, Night One
text:
Dear Diary,

Today we drove for {number} hours to get to Lake Wobble. My little brother sang the same song about {plural noun} the whole way there.

When we got to our campsite, Dad set up the tent. It took a long time because he kept {verb ending in ing} while he read the instructions upside down. Mom finally fixed it with a {noun} and some tape. Now our tent looks a little bit {adjective}, but it works.

For dinner we cooked hot dogs and a pot of {adjective} beans. Then we roasted marshmallows. Mine got too hot, so I blew on it {adverb}, and it tasted like a {noun}.

Tonight I can hear frogs, crickets, and something that goes "{sound}!" Mom says it is just an owl saying hello. I am going to {verb} until morning. Goodnight, Diary!

title: A Postcard from Camp Sunny Pines
text:
Dear Grandma,

Greetings from Camp Sunny Pines! The lake here is very {adjective}. The water is so cold that I {past tense verb} right out of it.

Yesterday we went on a nature hike. Our guide showed us a tree that is {number} years old and a rock shaped exactly like a {noun}. I collected seven {plural noun} for you. They are safe in my backpack.

This morning Dad tried to catch a fish. He waited {adverb} for two hours and caught a {noun} instead. He said it still counts. Mom took a picture.

Tomorrow we will {verb} in canoes. I will wear my life jacket and paddle like a {adjective} {animal}.

Love, your favorite grandchild

P.S. Please save me some {food}.

title: How to Set Up a Tent
text:
Setting up a tent is easy if you follow these steps. My dad wrote them after our last trip.

Step 1: Find a flat spot. Make sure there are no rocks, sticks, or {plural noun} on the ground.
Step 2: Unroll the tent. If a {animal} is already napping inside, choose a different spot.
Step 3: Push the poles through the loops. This part goes better if you hum a {adjective} song.
Step 4: Lift the tent up {adverb}. Ask a grown-up to hold the other side so it does not {verb}.
Step 5: Push in the stakes. You should have {number} stakes, but you will always find one in your {noun} later.
Step 6: Put your sleeping bag, pillow, and favorite {noun} inside.

Now step back and admire your tent. It should look {adjective} and strong. If it looks like a {noun} instead, go back to Step 1.

title: Pine Lake Camp News
text:
Good evening, campers! This is the Pine Lake Camp News.

Tonight was the big Marshmallow Roasting Contest. Twenty families gathered around the fire pit with their sticks and their {adjective} hats.

The first roaster, Mr. Hill, toasted his marshmallow until it was the size of a {noun}. The crowd {past tense verb}. Next, a girl named Rosie roasted {number} marshmallows at once while {verb ending in ing} on one foot. The judges were very impressed.

The winner was seven-year-old Sam, who toasted his marshmallow {adverb} and served it on a bed of {plural noun}. His prize was a golden {noun} and a blue ribbon.

In other news, someone left a {adjective} {noun} on the picnic table. If it is yours, please pick it up at the front office. That is all for tonight. Remember to brush your teeth and {verb} before bed!

title: Junior Ranger Fun Facts
text:
Hi! My name is Ava, and I am a Junior Forest Ranger. I earned my badge yesterday. Here are some fun facts I learned on our camping trip.

Fact 1: Squirrels hide nuts in the ground. They also hide {plural noun} when nobody is looking.
Fact 2: Pine cones open up when it is warm and close up when they feel {adjective}.
Fact 3: Owls can turn their heads almost all the way around. They do this so they can {verb} better.
Fact 4: If you listen {adverb} at night, you can hear the trees {verb ending in ing}.
Fact 5: Raccoons wash their food in the creek. Last night one washed my {noun}.
Fact 6: The tallest tree in our campground is taller than {number} school buses stacked on a {noun}.

That is all the facts I know so far. Next summer I want to earn my {adjective} badge. To get it, you have to catch a {noun} in a bug net.

title: Breakfast Menu at Campsite 12
text:
Good morning, campers! Chef Dad is cooking breakfast on the camp stove today. Here is the menu.

Pancakes: Fluffy, golden, and shaped like a {noun}. Served with syrup and a side of {plural noun}.
Scrambled Eggs: Stirred {adverb} with Grandpa's lucky spoon. Chef Dad says this makes them taste {adjective}.
Hot Cocoa: Topped with three marshmallows and a sprinkle of {food}.
The Mystery Special: Chef Dad will not tell us what is in it. It is {color}, and it {past tense verb} a little when Mom poked it.

Please wait in line and do not {verb} near the stove. Chef Dad gets very {adjective} when people touch his spatula.

After breakfast, everyone must wash their plate in the bucket and shout "{exclamation}!" to thank the chef.

title: Campground Talent Show Tonight
text:
Attention, all campers! The Shady Oaks Campground Talent Show is tonight at the big fire pit. It starts right after dinner.

Here is who will be performing:
- The Garcia twins will juggle {number} pine cones while {verb ending in ing}.
- Grandpa Lou will play the banjo and sing a song about his {adjective} canoe.
- Little Max will show everyone how he can {verb} with his eyes closed.
- The Park family dog, Biscuit, will balance a {noun} on his nose.

Ranger Kim will be the judge. The winner gets a {adjective} trophy made out of {plural noun}.

Please bring your own chair or a {noun} to sit on. Snacks will be served, including s'mores and {food}. If you would like to be in the show, sign up at the ranger station and practice {adverb}!

title: A Thank-You Letter to My Tent
text:
Dear Tent,

Thank you for keeping me cozy for {number} nights. You were the best tent in the whole campground, even when your zipper got stuck and Dad had to open you with a {noun}.

I am sorry about the time my brother {past tense verb} inside you. I am also sorry about the sticky {food} on your floor. We tried to clean it {adverb}, but some of it is still there.

You did a {adjective} job when the wind blew. You only wobbled a little bit, like a {adjective} {noun}.

Tomorrow we will fold you up and put you in the car next to the cooler and the {plural noun}. Please do not {verb} while we drive home. I will see you next summer!

Love,
Emma
